note: Depolarizing noise inserted after every gate (qml.insert(op=DepolarizingChannel, position='all')) on PennyLane's default.mixed density-matrix simulator, using the SAME weights trained noiselessly (default.qubit) elsewhere in this project — this measures robustness of an already-trained policy to hardware noise, not training under noise. noise_prob is a per-gate depolarizing probability, not a specific device's measured error rate; current superconducting NISQ hardware single-qubit gate error is roughly 0.05-0.5%, two-qubit (entangling) gate error roughly 0.5-2% depending on hardware generation — the swept range brackets this. reward_retained_pct = 100 * noisy_reward / noise_prob=0_reward on the SAME eval states; a value near 100% at realistic noise levels would suggest tolerance to near-term hardware noise, a sharp drop would suggest this ansatz needs error mitigation before real-hardware deployment. Simulation only — no physical quantum hardware used.
